definition: The prefix trans is Latin for "from the other" usually indicating a change of state. Transgender is an umbrella term used for people whose gender identity (identification as male, female, intersex, nonbinary, etc.) is different from what was assigned at birth. As explained by the National Center for Transgender Equality, a transgender girl or woman is a girl or woman whose sex assigned at birth was male, but who understands herself as female. A transgender boy or man is a boy or man whose sex assigned at birth was female, but who understands himself to be male. Some transgender people identify as neither male nor female, or as a combination of/among a spectrum of gender identities. There are many terms to describe gender identities beyond the binary of male and female, like androgynous, nonbinary, agender, or genderqueer. The opposite of transgender is cisgender, which describes people whose gender identity matches their assigned sex at birth. The Latin prefix cis is Latin for "same side as." Under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, discrimination based on sex is prohibited. This is enforced in the workplace by the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC). transfer agent / transgender Dictionary compilation | 26 September 2026
